verses.1: The Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Him,
verses.2: and saw that some of His disciples were eating bread with defiled — that is, unwashed — hands.
verses.3: (For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands carefully, holding to the tradition of the elders.
verses.4: And when they come from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other traditions they have received and hold, such as the washing of cups, pitchers, and bronze vessels.)
verses.5: The Pharisees and the scribes asked Him, "Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat with defiled hands?"
verses.6: And He said to them, "Isaiah prophesied rightly about you hypocrites, as it is written: 'This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.
verses.7: In vain do they worship Me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.'
verses.8: You leave the commandment of God and hold to the tradition of men."
verses.9: And He said to them, "You have a fine way of rejecting the commandment of God in order to keep your tradition.
verses.10: For Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and, 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must surely die.'
verses.11: But you say that if a man tells his father or mother, 'Whatever you would have received from me is Corban' — that is, given to God —
verses.12: you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother.
verses.13: Thus you nullify the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. And you do many things like this."
verses.14: And He called the crowd to Him again and said to them, "Listen to Me, all of you, and understand.
verses.15: There is nothing outside a person that by going into him can defile him, but the things that come out of a person are what defile him."
verses.16: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.
verses.17: When He had entered the house and left the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable.
verses.18: And He said to them, "Are you also without understanding? Do you not see that whatever goes into a person from outside cannot defile him,
verses.19: since it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and passes out into the sewer?" Thus He declared all foods clean.
verses.20: And He said, "What comes out of a person is what defiles him.
verses.21: For from within, out of the heart of man, come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery,
verses.22: greed, wickedness, deceit, sensuality, envy, slander, pride, and foolishness.
verses.23: All these evil things come from within, and they defile a person."
verses.24: And from there He arose and went away to the region of Tyre and Sidon. He entered a house and did not want anyone to know it, yet He could not be hidden.
verses.25: But immediately a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard about Him and came and fell at His feet.
verses.26: Now the woman was a Gentile, a Syrophoenician by birth. She begged Him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
verses.27: And He said to her, "Let the children be fed first, for it is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
verses.28: But she answered Him, "Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs."
verses.29: And He said to her, "For this saying you may go. The demon has left your daughter."
verses.30: And she went home and found the child lying on the bed, and the demon gone.
verses.31: Then He returned from the region of Tyre and went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the region of the Decapolis.
verses.32: And they brought to Him a man who was deaf and had a speech impediment, and they begged Him to lay His hand on him.
verses.33: And taking him aside from the crowd privately, He put His fingers into his ears, and after spitting, He touched his tongue.
verses.34: And looking up to heaven, He sighed and said to him, "Ephphatha," that is, "Be opened."
verses.35: And his ears were opened, his tongue was released, and he spoke plainly.
verses.36: And Jesus charged them to tell no one. But the more He charged them, the more zealously they proclaimed it.
verses.37: And they were astonished beyond measure, saying, "He has done all things well. He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak."
